findings.title: Plugin completion logs no longer include the trace ID
findings.body: The previous implementation explicitly extracted `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` and added it as the `traceID` log field. That extraction was removed, while the new contextual logger middleware only adds endpoint/plugin/data-source/user fields and does not add a trace ID. `FromContext` is therefore only being used to recover those contextual attributes, so completion logs for traced plugin calls lose the trace-to-log correlation field that was previously emitted. Preserve the explicit trace field or add the trace ID to the contextual attributes, and cover this with a traced-request logging test.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to the exported Logger interface breaks existing implementations
findings.body: `Logger` is an exported interface, and adding a required `FromContext(context.Context)` method is a source-compatible break for every external implementation, wrapper, fake, or mock that previously satisfied it. Those consumers will fail to compile even if they do not need contextual logging. Since this PR is described as a rename/chore, provide a backward-compatible path (for example, keep the original interface and use a separate optional contextual-logger interface/type assertion in the middleware) or explicitly handle the API-versioning/migration impact.
